items.title: Plans to replace plaza with apartment buildings in Mississauga revised
items.summary: A proposal to replace a plaza with a residential development in Mississauga returns next month with a few changes. The plans for an old plaza at 1225 Dundas St. , west of Dixie Road, have changed a few times. The plaza is home to a few businesses such as Danforth Food Market, Baituna Furniture and Spoon and Fork. The plaza at at 1225 Dundas St. E. Photo: Google Maps In 2022, developers submitted an application to build a 12-storey residential apartment building with 462 units with ground-floor retail and 34 townhouses. In 2024, the height increased to an 18-storey terraced building with two point tower components connected by a shared nine-storey podium. The heights have now been lowered, and the plan is for two 16-storey apartment buildings connected by a six-storey podium from developers Stephen-Mitchell Reality Limited, Whitehorn Investments Limited, Lynrob Investments Limited, Richco Investments Limited and Tobdele Investments Limited, according to reports submitted to the City of Mississauga. A rendering shows plans for the apartment buildings.

items.title: Lane closed on historic bridge to allow restoration work to proceed in Mississauga
items.summary: Motorists are being alerted to a lane closure on a historic bridge located in the north end of Mississauga. Peel Region officials said one lane will be closed to traffic on the Old Derry Road bridge today through Friday to allow restoration work to take place on the structure. The bridge, which crosses over the Credit River, is located on Old Derry Road between Historic Trail and Credit Valley Conservation Road in the historic Meadowvale Village area of Mississauga. Peel officials said traffic control measures will be in place in the affected area over the next three days. Earlier this year, the City of Mississauga launched an environmental assessment (EA) study for Old Derry Road, which runs through the historic community of Meadowvale Village. ” Among the improvements being considered are pavement rehabilitation, new cycling infrastructure and the repair or replacement of existing bridge structures, including the Old Derry Road bridge over the Credit River. The Old Derry Road bridge is a designated heritage structure within the Meadowvale Village Heritage Conservation District and serves as a scenic gateway into the village. Built in 1930, the bridge is considered historically significant for its design and character.

items.title: Mayor Parrish Says AMO Conference Meetings Secured New Housing Funding for Mississauga
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish says a series of meetings in Ottawa this week has secured new provincial funding for housing in Mississauga and Peel Region, though she did not disclose the exact amount. INsauga reports Parrish described the city's delegation as well received at the 2026 Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference, where she was joined by Deputy Mayor Matt Mahoney, Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca, City Manager Geoff Wright and other senior city officials. The delegation met with Ontario cabinet ministers, opposition party leaders, MPPs and industry stakeholders to advocate for Mississauga's priorities, according to the city. Beyond affordable housing, INsauga reports those priorities included strengthening public transit, supporting economic growth and trade resilience, addressing flood prevention and infrastructure needs, securing a fairer police funding formula for Peel, and investing in arts, culture and sport infrastructure. City officials also raised concerns about electric scooter safety in Mississauga, an issue INsauga notes has come up repeatedly at council over the past two years.

items.title: Eight Studios and $1 Million in Annual Revenue Anchor Mississauga's Push to Stay a Film Hub
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city is doubling down on its identity as a film and television production hub as growing incentives in the United States put pressure on Ontario's industry. Mississauga.com reports the city is home to eight major film studios with more than one million square feet of combined stage space, including CBS Stages Canada on Matheson Boulevard East. The city earned close to one million dollars in revenue from film and television production in 2021, and officials describe that activity as an important contributor to the local economy. In June 2026, according to Mississauga.com, city council adopted a strategy called The Creative Advantage, a transformational action plan meant to increase Mississauga's appeal to creative businesses and investment, including in film. Industry officials cited by Mississauga.com caution that the broader competitive landscape facing the sector will still be shaped largely by policy and investment decisions made at the provincial and federal levels, not just by the city's own initiatives.

items.title: Paul Coffey Park's Flight Garden Gets a Full-Size Tribute to Malton's Avro Arrow
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a replica of the Avro Arrow CF-105 has been permanently installed in the Flight Garden at Paul Coffey Park, with an unveiling ceremony planned in partnership with the Malton Business Improvement Area. The city says Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart, other members of council, Malton BIA chair Sam Kohli and project sponsors are set to take part in the outdoor ceremony marking the jet's official unveiling. According to the city, the project commemorates the supersonic aircraft that was designed and built in the 1950s in Mississauga's Malton neighbourhood, once the site of the Avro aircraft plant. The City of Mississauga notes the original Avro Arrow was the largest plane of its kind when built, measuring 55 feet wide and 72 feet long, and was known for its superior speed, lower weight and ability to carry more payload than comparable aircraft of its era. The city also highlights several firsts credited to the Arrow's design, including early use of digital computers and computer numerical control machining, along with computer-controlled navigation, weapons release and electronic countermeasures technology.

items.title: Mystery Film Shoot at Iceland Mississauga Sparks Heated Rivalry Season 2 Speculation
items.summary: According to NOW Toronto, filming has begun on the second season of the Canadian queer hockey series Heated Rivalry, and fans are speculating that part of the production may be happening in Mississauga. NOW Toronto reports the show's team posted an Instagram photo of a film slate labeled Day 1 on Monday, confirming shooting had started, around the same time social media users noticed an unannounced production filming at Iceland Mississauga, an Olympic-sized ice rink in the city's west end. A customer service representative at the arena confirmed to NOW Toronto by phone that a production was indeed filming on location on August 17, though the representative said staff had no details on who booked the space, since scheduling comes through a third-party organization. NOW Toronto notes there is no actual confirmation that the mystery shoot was connected to Heated Rivalry, and the show does not currently appear listed as filming in Mississauga according to the industry tracking site Production List. Even without confirmation, the overlapping timing has been enough to fuel speculation among fans watching for signs of the show's return.

items.title: Peel police sign 'first-of-its-kind' pact with Human Rights Commission to implement dozens of anti-racism recommendations
items.summary: The agreement will see a new independent oversight process to help drive “meaningful, measurable change” against systemic racism. Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah lauded the agreement as a concrete step in building trust with residents. The force started consultations to help address systemic racism back in 2020. A new independent body will be tasked with guiding the implementation of more than 65 recommendations to address systemic racism within Peel police, after a “first-of-its-kind” agreement was struck between the service, its board and the Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC). The binding arbitration accord, announced Tuesday, aims to enact a wide range of recommendations to eliminate racial discrimination, such as the further prohibition of police street checks and carding the use of de-escalation techniques, and emphasizing organizational change through hiring and training. ” “Policing must be fair, equitable, and free from systemic bias. This first-of-its-kind agreement demonstrates our leadership in driving meaningful, measurable change through transparent, independent oversight,” he said in a statement. The three organizations say the recommendations were made by the OHRC through the Human Rights Project, which began in February 2020.

items.title: Trapeze Duo Behind Canada's First Quadruple Somersault Set to Perform in Mississauga This Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Royal Canadian Circus is bringing a newly set Canadian first with it when it arrives in Mississauga this month, days after a milestone performance in Scarborough. Circus officials said trapeze duo The Flying Poema completed Canada's first-ever quadruple somersault during the closing weekend of a 10-day run at Scarborough Town Centre. INsauga reports officials described the move as an extremely rare feat that only a handful of performers worldwide have ever landed, and said The Flying Poema plans to attempt it again at future stops on the tour. The circus, currently marking its 52nd anniversary Canadian tour, will set up in the parking lot of Dixie Outlet Mall in Mississauga's east end from August 21 to 30, following a similar 10-day stay at the same mall in August 2025. INsauga notes the Mississauga stop is part of an all-new 2026 production that has already toured through Hamilton, Brampton, Newmarket, Markham and Vaughan, with Burlington next up on the schedule from September 3 to 7.

items.title: Studio.89 Will Shut Its Eglinton Avenue Storefront But Keep Its Community Programs Running
items.summary: According to INsauga, Studio.89, a non-profit fair trade and vegan cafe that has also served as a community hub in Mississauga, announced on Instagram that it will close its brick-and-mortar location on September 14. INsauga reports the cafe has operated at 2520 Eglinton Avenue West, offering espresso drinks, coffee, smoothies, sandwiches and treats as a social enterprise that funnels sales toward its social, cultural and environmental mission. This isn't the first time the organization has faced a financial crunch, INsauga notes, pointing to a 2018 fundraising push that brought in a $50,000 donation to help keep the cafe's doors open. Even after the physical space closes, Studio.89 says it plans to keep running its community programming at venues across Mississauga, according to INsauga. Those programs include initiatives focused on art as a tool for social change, climate action, youth leadership, connections between youth and seniors, and job skills training.

items.title: Chef Matty Matheson's Maker Pizza Chain Set to Open Its Fifth Location in Mississauga
items.summary: According to WhatNow, Maker Pizza, the pizza chain founded by celebrity chef Matty Matheson and business partner Shlomo Buchler, is set to open a new location at 181 City Centre Drive in Mississauga in late August. WhatNow reports the Mississauga shop will mark the brand's fifth location since it launched in 2015 with an original spot on Cameron Street. The new store joins existing Maker Pizza locations on Cameron Street, Bayview Avenue and Carlaw Avenue in Toronto, along with a Bathurst Street shop in Thornhill. According to the report, the menu sells pizza by the slice or whole pie, with specialty options including Siena Margherita, Napoli Dynamite, Dr. Pepperoni and Tropic Thunder. WhatNow notes the shop also offers a range of dips, such as creamy garlic, dill ranch and spicy creamy garlic, along with wings and garlic fingers.
